'''Jack Gorski''' (1931-2006) was an American [[reproductive medicine|reproductive biologist]] who was a pioneer in [[estrogen]] [[endocrinology]].<ref name="In Memoriam">{{cite journal | title=In Memoriam: Jack Gorski, Ph.D. 1931–2006 | journal=[[Biology of Reproduction]]  | volume=78 | issue=3| year=2008 | pages= 565 |doi = 10.1095/biolreprod.108.068007 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
Jack Gorski was born in [[Green Bay, Wisconsin]], earned a B.S. degree from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] and a Ph.D. degree from the [[Washington State University]]. In 1958, he started postdoctoral research on the action of estrogens at [[McArdle Laboratory|Mcardle Laboratory for Cancer Research]], University of Wisconsin. Hence, he continued to expand his interest in [[steroid]] biochemistry. He found [[estrogen receptor]]s almost at the same time as [[Elwood V. Jensen]] and laid the foundation for the study of [[steroid receptor|steroid nuclear receptor]]s. In 1986 he was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and in 1993 a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="In Memoriam"/>
